name: Asante Traditional Buildings
description: In the hills northeast of Kumasi, Ghana, ten small shrine houses are all that survive of the Asante buildings from the empire's 18th- and 19th-century golden age. They are built from earth, wood and straw, and were once used as places of worship and spiritual practice. Most Asante architecture was destroyed during British occupation, so these fragile buildings are rare survivors of a vanished world.
